entries.reason: Mounts the provider's React context around the app. The port covers what the product asks of a provider, not the provider's own component tree, so the mount is part of a swap rather than a leak the port can absorb.

The only browser importer of the provider's sign-in and sign-up hooks. It turns them into this product's own auth contract (start with email, submit password, submit code, resend, start a provider, finish the redirect), so /login, /signup and the SSO callback name no vendor and a swap replaces this file alone.
The browser composition root. It is where the provider's hooks are chosen, and it exports useSession, useCurrentUser and useSignOut in this product's shapes so no component names the vendor.
The browser composition root for the imperative token read the service modules use outside React. Kept out of the hooks module so it carries no use client boundary.

Enterprise SSO is brokered by the provider's enterprise-connections product, which has no equivalent in the port. sso_connections stores the provider's connection id and the activation gate depends on it, so moving this is its own slice.
